messages.subject: Does vim-R-plugin use the Clipboard
messages.body_plain:
hi,
first of all thanks for this great plugin. I've been using it happily for nearly two years now!

I've been working with the plugin on linux, mac and recently windows but I'm not quite sure how the communication actually works.
Today I noticed that the r-function readClipboard() will always return "readClipboard()" when sending it from vim to R (on windows) and that it actually overrides the clipboard.

Is there a way to avoid this behavior or does the plugin actually communicate via the clipboard?

Best,
stephan

messages.subject: Re: Does vim-R-plugin use the Clipboard
messages.body_plain: The Vim-R-plugin uses the clipboard on Windows, but not on Linux or Mac. On Windows, it sets the clipboard, paste its contents into R Console and, then, restores the clipboard data to the previous value. Please, see: http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/vimrcom.pdf

messages.subject: After closing the R console with ",rq", Vim goes haywire.
messages.subject_clean: After closing the R console with ",rq", Vim goes haywire.
messages.body_plain:
After closing the R console with the command ",rq", Vim goes haywire.

When I try to pass into command mode with the "Escape" key, I get the following output "^[".
The arrow keys also no longer work,
For example, the up arrow gives the following output: "[OA".
Since I cannot pass into command mode, I cannot quit Vim and have to close the terminal.

How can I correct this issue?
Before closing the R console, everything works fine.
Everything also works fine if I close the R console by switching panes, and typing "q()".

messages.body_plain:
Hello, with the Rcpp package becoming so much popular I was wondering if you were planning to support some kind of C++ completion support.
Personally I tend to write a lot of C++ to speedup some R code and the ability to complete STL or whatever is a huge gain.
I was wondering whether you thought about using YouCompleteMe for C++ and R completion all together (I know some people are using it).

I happy to elaborate if you are remotely interested in the idea.

Regards and thank you for the plugin

messages.subject: Re: Vim R plugin and C++
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I don't plan to support C++ because I don't use it with R. In fact, I have to focus in my real work (social sciences) and slow down the development of the plugin and other software. I don't use YouCompleteMe, but perhaps the tip in the plugin documentation about the use of rtags is useful (see http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/r-plugin.html#r-plugin-tagsfile).

Note that the Vim-R-plugin can be extended or modified by code written by other people (see http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/r-plugin.html#vimrplugin_source). Alternatively, if someone writes a pull request to https://github.com/jcfaria/Vim-R-plugin, I may apply it.

Regards,

--
Jakson
